comment: The three-layer model (governance layer, runtime layer, content/application layer) introduced in lines 419–431 is editorially confusing because it does not map to the document's overall architecture framework. Earlier sections presumably describe the architecture using a component model (client registry, terminology service, etc.) or a layered model (business, data, application, technology — per TOGAF or OpenHIE). Now a new "three layers" model appears without explaining how it relates to those existing layers. Is the governance layer part of the business architecture? Is the runtime layer the technology architecture? Is SGI an application component or a cross-cutting concern?

public.text: The three-layer model (governance layer, runtime layer, content/application layer) introduced in lines 419–431 is editorially confusing because it does not map to the document's overall architecture framework. Earlier sections presumably describe the architecture using a component model (client registry, terminology service, etc.) or a layered model (business, data, application, technology — per TOGAF or OpenHIE). Now a new "three layers" model appears without explaining how it relates to those existing layers. Is the governance layer part of the business architecture? Is the runtime layer the technology architecture? Is SGI an application component or a cross-cutting concern?
public.suggestedRevision: Add an explicit mapping paragraph after line 431: "These three layers can be understood in relation to the architecture framework used throughout this document as follows: The governance layer corresponds to the business architecture processes and the governance structures defined in Sections 3.4.3 and 3.4.4. The runtime layer corresponds to the application and technology architecture components — specifically the Terminology Service, Logical Information Model Repository, and their underlying infrastructure (Section [X.X]). The content and application layer corresponds to the business use cases and the consuming applications that implement them. SGI spans the governance and runtime layers: it is a business process (governance) that operates on application components (runtime) and is triggered by content layer feedback." Then add a figure showing the three SGI layers mapped to the document's primary architecture framework.
